title: Temperature-tendency interactions left a negative Pacific volume slope contrast in 1980-2024 fits
abstract: We tested whether the recent direction of surface temperature change accounts for unequal warm and cold slopes for later Pacific warm water volume change. We used frozen NOAA GODAS and ERSSTv5 snapshots and 531 monthly starts from April 1980 to June 2024. The base fit controlled for starting volume, month, time and prior three-month temperature and volume changes. Adding temperature-by-tendency terms gave a warm-minus-cold slope contrast of -1.28 at zero tendency, in units of 10^14 cubic metres per degree C. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was -2.12 to -0.45. The paired change from the base was -0.11, with limits of -0.50 to +0.24. Thus these interaction terms did not clearly change the contrast. A spatial temperature control left an adjusted interval across zero. This is a model-dependent association, not a causal effect or a forecast test. One revised ocean product, few climate cycles and fixed model terms limit inference. The package includes original code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and a numerical audit. External source and monthly records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Warm-minus-cold slopes at zero temperature tendency and paired changes after adding two interaction terms. Bars give conditional 95% year-block intervals. The spatial check has an interval across zero.
